title: Programming Languages: Short Answer
instructions: Reminder: high-level code hides hardware details, while low-level code is close to what the CPU does.

questions.prompt: In your own words, what does it mean for a language to be high-level versus low-level?
answers: High-level code is easier for humans to read and hides hardware details. Low-level code, such as assembly or machine code, is close to the instructions the CPU executes and is harder for humans to write.

questions.prompt: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of writing in a high-level language instead of a low-level one.
answers: An advantage is that high-level code is usually faster and easier to read, write, and debug. A disadvantage is that it can provide less direct hardware control and may be less efficient than carefully written low-level code.
